Updated read with SLOOS overlay:
- Baseline: The May 1 FOMC statement is still cautious-hawkish: solid activity and strong labor markets, explicit “lack of further progress” on disinflation, no cuts until “greater confidence,” and a modestly dovish offset via slowing QT (Treasury cap to $25B; agency MBS cap unchanged).
- SLOOS signal: Banks report continued tightening across C&I and consumer credit (credit cards, auto), with wider spreads and tougher nonprice terms (higher credit score requirements, tighter limits), and weaker loan demand. CRE standards remain notably tighter (lower LTVs, higher DSCRs, shorter IO periods, reduced market areas), with banks citing economic outlook, risk tolerance, sector-specific issues, and vacancy/rent dynamics. This indicates bank credit is still a headwind.
- Implication for tone: The ongoing credit tightening and softer loan demand temper the hawkish edge of the statement by reinforcing that financial conditions are restrictive even without further rate hikes. The QT slowdown aligns with risk management amid tight credit and CRE pressures. Net result is still modestly hawkish due to inflation language and “higher-for-longer” guidance, but nudged closer to neutral by SLOOS.
